Introduction
With the rapid development of the automobile industry, auto-
motive lightweight materials have become an important
research topic. Among them, FeeMneAleC steel has good
corrosion resistance, low density and excellent comprehensive
mechanical properties, having great application prospect in the
fields of weight reduction, collision safety and the complex
working conditions of the automobiles structure [1e4]. In
addition, thermoplastic deformation can effectively refine the
grain size and improve the properties of forgings and micro-
structure. In the field of actual production, the microstructure is
primarily controlled by way of thermal machining. Dynamic
recrystallization (DRX) is beneficial to grain refinement and
homogenization and is an important deformation mechanism
to improve the microstructure and properties within the hot
working process [5e7]. Therefore, in-depth studies on the
microstructure evolution and DRX behavior of FeeMneAleC
steel are of great significance for the formulation and optimi-
zation of the hot forging process of the steel.
At present, reports on FeeMneAleC steel primarily focus
on smelting, heat treatment and mechanical properties. For
example, Moon et al. [8] studied Fee30Mn-10.5Al-1.1C-(0e5)
Mo steel. It was found that Mo-enriched

three different methods. It was found that the distribution of

form than that of the samples after air and water cooling; this,
the corresponding mechanical properties were superior.
However, the research reports on the hot deformation
behavior of low-density high-strength FeeMneAleC steel are
not thorough enough. In this paper, the microstructure evo-
lution law and DRX behavior of the steel were studied using a
thermal simulation compression experiment and metallo-
graphic observation. The flow stress curve characteristics of
the steel were analyzed through the experimental data, and
the dynamic recrystallization activation energy and Z pa-
rameters were calculated. The critical strain conditions for
DRX were determined based on the Cingara-McQueen equa-
tion [10]. Functional relationships between rheological stress
curve characteristic values (critical strain/stress, peak strain/
stress and steady-state strain/stress) and the dimensionless
parameter Zener-Hollomon [11] were established. A dynamic
recrystallization state diagram was drawn and a dynamic
recrystallization average grain size prediction model was
constructed. The research results provide theoretical support
for the determination of the hot forging processes parameters
as well as the numerical simulation of the hot forming of low-
density high-strength Fe-Mn-Al-C steel

conditions for the proper functioning of their materials/de-
